Transfer and promotion

Source: R/download.R
getaca-transfer.Rd

Bytes land in .tmp/, are sized, hashed, and only then moved into the cache. An interrupted transfer can never appear as a valid cached resource, and a failed transfer never touches a copy that was already good.

Details

The temporary file is named after the declared checksum, so an interrupted download resumes on the next attempt rather than starting over. That matters when the resource is measured in gigabytes.

getaca drives the transfer itself, over the curl multi interface, rather than handing a URL to a function that returns when it is done. What that buys is the response status before the first byte is written, and a count of the bytes as they arrive. The first decides where they go; the second is what getaca-progress reports.

When a transfer is given up on

A transfer is given up on for standing still, never for taking long. A connection that takes longer than getaca.connect_seconds, 30 by default, to open, or that delivers nothing for getaca.stall_seconds, 60 by default, is dropped. One that keeps delivering runs for as long as the file takes. getaca.timeout limits a whole transfer, in seconds, and is off unless set.

A connection that dropped after delivering bytes is resumed on the same mirror, for as long as each attempt gets further. A mirror that answers that it is busy (HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 or 504) is asked again after a wait that doubles from two seconds, or after the interval its Retry-After header names, and never after more than a minute. Attempts that move nothing are counted against getaca.retries, 3 by default, after which the next mirror is tried. A mirror that never answered, or answered that the file is not there, is not asked twice.

Several files at once

The parts of a series, and the resources of one getaca_prefetch() call, share up to getaca.connections connections, 4 by default. A file two of them name is transferred once.

Each setting is also read from an environment variable, GETACA_STALL_SECONDS for getaca.stall_seconds and so on, when the option is unset.
